taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Tridens eragrostoides normalized to current accepted Triplasiella eragrostoides.
look_here_first: LOVEGRASS TRIDENS: a fine open, arching and widely spreading lovegrass-like panicle with tiny dispersed spikelets, unlike compact narrow Tridens heads. Confirmation requires a mature 3-veined lemma, glumes and ligule under magnification, not merely a large airy grass panicle. Historical synonym Tridens eragrostoides is NOT another canonical species.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Poaceae: use growth habit, ligule, panicle architecture, spikelet form, lemma hairs and awns. For this old Tridens complex, panicle openness/color and current genus placement are especially useful.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: The airy lovegrass-like seedhead is the main cue. It is much more open than white tridens and now belongs in Triplasiella.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Same rooted plant with wide open panicle and leaf collar
One mature spikelet 20x showing actual lemma nerves and florets

items.caption: FOLLOW THE FOREGROUND STEM: long, thin, spreading branches bear small reddish-brown spikelets over the hand. The conspicuous bristly seedhead in the upper-right background belongs to another plant; do not count it as a Triplasiella structure. The hand is not a calibrated millimeter scale, and individual lemma nerves, glumes, and ligule cannot be diagnosed from this image.
